communication_style.correction_style: States the changed constraint directly, such as a later meeting end time or a newly firm hotel budget, without revisiting settled details.
communication_style.decision_pattern: Eliminates options that fail core timing or routing needs, compares remaining prices, and asks one or two follow-up questions about hotel amenities or location before deciding.
communication_style.request_pattern: Provides fixed dates and hard schedule constraints first, then asks for a small ranked shortlist with the meaningful tradeoffs called out.

habit_interactions: For flights, workable timing and nonstop routing define the acceptable set; lowest price ranks that set, while Delta acts as a tie-breaker or near-tie preference rather than overriding a materially better itinerary.
The afternoon return preference often preserves a final morning for client work or leisure, but explicit checkout, meeting, or home-arrival needs remain trip-specific constraints.
For hotels, the applicable rating floor establishes a quality baseline, while pool and fitness facilities help distinguish otherwise suitable properties.
Beach proximity is activated only on coastal leisure trips and competes with budget and rating rather than becoming a general hotel-location rule.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat this as a soft default; departures close to afternoon may be considered when true afternoon options are limited or unattractive.
habits.condition: When booking or comparing round-trip flights and selecting the return leg departure time.
habits.default_action: Present return-flight options departing in the afternoon first and let the user choose among them.
habits.exception_condition: Do not generalize this return-leg preference to outbound legs, and follow any explicit timing requirement for the current trip.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat this as a preference rather than an absolute requirement unless the user explicitly says no layovers for the current trip.
habits.condition: When searching for outbound or return flights, prioritize nonstop options.
habits.default_action: Search for and present a nonstop itinerary first.
habits.exception_condition: If no suitable nonstop flight is available, a one-stop option may be acceptable, but confirm the tradeoff before booking.
habits.name: Prefer nonstop flights
habits.preference_value: Nonstop flights are generally preferred.

habits.boundary_condition: This is a soft preference: the evidence supports Delta as a favored option, not as the only acceptable airline or an always-first choice over every other preferred carrier.
habits.condition: When choosing among flight carriers and Delta is available while also satisfying the trip's schedule, route, price, and stop constraints.
habits.default_action: Search for or present Delta options as part of the preferred carrier set, and favor Delta when it is otherwise comparable to alternatives.
habits.exception_condition: Use another acceptable carrier when Delta is unavailable, materially worse, or does not meet the current trip constraints.
habits.name: Delta as a soft preferred carrier option
habits.preference_value: Delta is a preferred airline to include in the flight shortlist, but not an exclusive carrier requirement.
habits.scope_condition: Applies when Maya compares carriers for trips originating in Minneapolis and Delta has an itinerary that is reasonably comparable on schedule, route, and price.

habits.boundary_condition: Do not let price override explicit requirements such as Wi-Fi, acceptable layover length, nonstop service when requested, or required departure and return timing.
habits.condition: When comparing flights that meet the trip's required timing, connectivity, and onboard-feature needs.
habits.default_action: Rank acceptable options by price and choose the cheapest one.
habits.exception_condition: Choose a more expensive option when the cheapest violates a stated must-have or has an unacceptably long or inconvenient layover.
habits.name: Cheapest acceptable flight
habits.preference_value: Prefer the lowest-priced flight that still satisfies essential itinerary and amenity constraints.
habits.scope_condition: Applies after Maya's current trip timing, routing, and any stated onboard requirements have defined an acceptable domestic flight shortlist; she then prefers its lowest-priced option.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat the pool and exercise facility as the durable core preference and the hot tub as a softer additional preference. Do not infer indoor versus outdoor pool requirements, a specific pool type, or unrelated room amenities unless stated for the current trip.
habits.condition: When choosing or comparing hotels based on wellness or recreation amenities.
habits.default_action: Prioritize hotels that offer both a pool and an on-site fitness center, gym, or comparable exercise facility; among otherwise suitable options, prefer one that also has a hot tub.
habits.exception_condition: Relax the hot-tub preference when it materially limits suitable options, and relax either core amenity when the user explicitly waives it or stronger current-trip constraints favor another hotel.
habits.name: prefers_hotels_with_pool_fitness_and_optional_hot_tub
habits.preference_value: Prefer hotels with both a pool and an on-site fitness facility, with a hot tub as an additional preference when available.
habits.scope_condition: Applies to Maya's multi-night work and leisure hotel stays, where a pool and on-site fitness facility support her recurring exercise routine and a hot tub is an additional preference.

habits.boundary_condition: Use a 3.5 minimum when the search is explicitly budget-focused. Apply either threshold only to the rating metric under discussion, and do not conflate hotel class, Google ratings, and customer-review ratings.
habits.condition: When a hotel search calls for a well-rated property and frames the stay as nice, upscale, resort-style, or explicitly budget-focused.
habits.default_action: Filter or prioritize options meeting a 4.0 minimum for nice, upscale, or resort-style searches, and identify the rating source when known.
habits.exception_condition: Follow any newly stated threshold or metric. If no suitable option meets the applicable floor while satisfying more important trip constraints, ask before relaxing it.
habits.name: contextual_hotel_rating_floor
habits.preference_value: Prefer hotels rated at least 4.0 when seeking a nice, upscale, or resort-style stay; for explicitly budget-focused searches, prefer at least 3.5.
habits.scope_condition: Applies when Maya explicitly frames a hotel search as nice, upscale, or resort-style, using a 4.0 rating floor, or as budget-focused, using a 3.5 floor for the named rating metric.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat walking distance as the reusable threshold; use a stricter walk-time limit only when the current request explicitly supplies one
habits.condition: When searching for a hotel in a coastal or beach-oriented area
habits.default_action: Prioritize properties on the beach or close enough to walk while also filtering to the trip's stated budget
habits.exception_condition: Do not apply this preference to non-coastal trips or when the current trip names a different location priority
habits.name: Prefer beach-proximate hotels
habits.preference_value: A hotel on or near the beach, ideally within walking distance
habits.scope_condition: Applies on Maya's beach-oriented trips with her partner, where she repeatedly looks for a hotel on or near the beach and normally treats walking distance as the proximity threshold.

longitudinal_plan.travel_tempo: About nine client-travel episodes and two leisure episodes per year, with additional short sessions for revisions, comparisons, seat or schedule follow-up, and occasional disrupted-trip replanning over roughly four years.
longitudinal_plan.typical_episode_shape: A typical episode spans 3 to 7 sessions: initial constraint gathering, flight shortlist refinement, hotel comparison, a booking-stage confirmation, and sometimes a later change. Work episodes are compact; coastal leisure episodes include more iterative hotel and location tradeoffs. Some sessions should be unrelated factual follow-ups or current-trip exceptions so the history does not probe every habit mechanically.

For family leisure hotels, included breakfast is more consistently useful than a balcony. The balcony remains a background differentiator for coastal stays and should not displace a better overall hotel.
Window seating recurs across trip types, but family seating needs or unavailable seat selection can supersede it for a particular itinerary.

habits.default_action: Prioritize departure options in the afternoon.
habits.exception_condition: Use another departure period when explicitly requested or when no workable afternoon option is available.
habits.name: Prefer afternoon departures
habits.preference_value: Afternoon flight departures preferred
habits.scope_condition: Across work and family trips when Danielle has discretion over the departure period and no event, school, or same-day obligation requires another time.

habits.boundary_condition: Apply this only when comparing connecting itineraries; do not infer a general preference for either nonstop flights or flights with a layover.
habits.condition: When evaluating flight itineraries with connections.
habits.default_action: Prioritize itineraries with at most one layover and a short connection that permits a practical transfer and brief break.
habits.exception_condition: Follow explicit current-trip requirements for a different number or duration of stops.
habits.name: flight_connection_limit_preference
habits.preference_value: When a flight connection is needed, prefer no more than one short layover.
habits.scope_condition: Across domestic trips when the viable flight set includes connecting itineraries.

habits.boundary_condition: Do not let price override explicit requirements such as Wi-Fi, acceptable layover length, nonstop service when requested, or required departure and return timing.
habits.condition: When comparing flights that meet the trip's required timing, connectivity, and onboard-feature needs.
habits.default_action: Rank acceptable options by price and choose the cheapest one.
habits.exception_condition: Choose a more expensive option when the cheapest violates a stated must-have or has an unacceptably long or inconvenient layover.
habits.name: Cheapest acceptable flight
habits.preference_value: Prefer the lowest-priced flight that still satisfies essential itinerary and amenity constraints.
habits.scope_condition: Especially for nonprofit-funded work travel, and also for family travel, after current itinerary and amenity requirements have been satisfied.

habits.boundary_condition: Applies only to seat location. If seat selection is unavailable at booking or is deferred until check-in, note that limitation and try to secure a window seat at the earliest available time.
habits.condition: When booking or selecting seats for flights where a seat location preference can be applied.
habits.default_action: Prefer or request a window seat by default.
habits.exception_condition: Use a different seat only if the user specifies another seat preference, needs a different seating arrangement, or no acceptable window seat is available.
habits.name: prefers_window_seat_on_flights
habits.preference_value: window seat
habits.scope_condition: When Danielle is selecting her own seat on a work or leisure flight and seat location is available for selection.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat this as a soft preference because the evidence ranges from tentative interest to a direct requirement.
habits.condition: When evaluating or booking a hotel.
habits.default_action: Prioritize hotels with free breakfast when available, and verify whether breakfast is included if the listing is unclear.
habits.exception_condition: Do not reject an otherwise suitable hotel solely because free breakfast is unavailable unless the user makes it mandatory for the current booking; do not infer requirements about breakfast type or quality.
habits.name: prefer_included_hotel_breakfast
habits.preference_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
habits.scope_condition: When comparing hotels for work trips with early meetings or venue calls, and as a lesser convenience during family stays.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat the balcony as a soft preference rather than a strict requirement; a first-floor room can be acceptable without one
habits.condition: When selecting a hotel room
habits.default_action: Prioritize rooms with a balcony when available
habits.exception_condition: Do not reject an otherwise suitable hotel solely because a balcony is unavailable
habits.name: hotel_room_balcony_preference
habits.preference_value: Prefer a room with a balcony
habits.scope_condition: When selecting a room for a coastal or otherwise scenic family leisure stay where Danielle expects to spend meaningful downtime at the hotel.

longitudinal_plan.travel_tempo: Roughly twelve to fourteen trips per year, with frequent short work episodes, several family-planning episodes, and occasional follow-up sessions for schedule changes, seat selection, or hotel verification.
longitudinal_plan.typical_episode_shape: Most trips unfold over two to four sessions: an initial constraint-setting request, a comparison or refinement session, a selection step, and sometimes a later adjustment. Annual coastal vacations generate longer hotel-comparison threads, while routine work trips are shorter and more repetitive.

persona.household: Lives with her spouse and their 14-year-old daughter; the family takes several school-break trips, including a coastal vacation most years.
persona.name: Danielle Brooks
persona.occupation: Corporate partnerships director for a national youth arts nonprofit
persona.planning_behavior: She starts with fixed event dates or school calendars, then filters flights by usable departure time and connection quality before comparing acceptable options by price. She usually handles flight details quickly but spends more time comparing hotels for family vacations, where the setting and room experience matter more. For work stays, she values included breakfast because mornings often begin with early venue calls or meetings.
persona.travel_pattern: Danielle travels about once a month for sponsor meetings, fundraising events, and program showcases in major U.S. cities. Work trips usually last two or three nights, while family trips are less frequent and planned farther ahead. Her routes vary enough that connections are sometimes necessary, and nonprofit travel budgets make price important once an itinerary is workable.

travel_contexts.frequency: Eight to ten domestic trips per year
travel_contexts.typical_needs: Fixed event windows, practical connections, controlled airfare, a reliable seat preference, and breakfast that simplifies early work mornings

travel_contexts.frequency: Three or four trips per year, usually around school breaks
travel_contexts.typical_needs: Flexible flight shopping and more deliberate hotel comparison, with balconies especially appealing on coastal or scenic stays

travel_contexts.frequency: Usually one longer trip each year
travel_contexts.typical_needs: A comfortable hotel stay where outdoor room space contributes meaningfully to the vacation experience

communication_style.decision_style: Prefers a short ranked set of workable options and asks targeted follow-up questions when a hotel claim or flight constraint is unclear.
communication_style.request_pattern: Usually supplies dates and fixed commitments first, then asks for a compact comparison with the important tradeoffs made explicit.

habit_interactions: For work flights, nonstop routing and a later return departure protect schedule reliability and usable time; Delta and a window seat help distinguish otherwise comparable options but do not override the itinerary.
For the annual coastal trip, beach walkability and the applicable upscale or resort rating floor work together as the main hotel screen.
The queen-bed default applies to shared personal hotel rooms, including the coastal vacation, while explicit room arrangements still control any particular booking.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat this as a preference rather than an absolute requirement unless the user explicitly says no layovers for the current trip.
habits.condition: When searching for outbound or return flights, prioritize nonstop options.
habits.default_action: Search for and present a nonstop itinerary first.
habits.exception_condition: If no suitable nonstop flight is available, a one-stop option may be acceptable, but confirm the tradeoff before booking.
habits.name: Prefer nonstop flights
habits.preference_value: Nonstop flights are generally preferred.
habits.scope_condition: Recurring domestic museum work trips where fixed access windows make itinerary simplicity valuable.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat the preference as a flexible later-day window ranging from afternoon to after 6:00 p.m., not as a fixed cutoff
habits.condition: When selecting a return flight and multiple departure times are available
habits.default_action: Prioritize return options departing in the afternoon or evening
habits.exception_condition: Use another departure period when the traveler explicitly requests it for the current trip or no later-day option is workable
habits.name: Prefer later-day return flights
habits.preference_value: Afternoon or evening return departures
habits.scope_condition: Return legs from museum work trips when the final day's duties end early enough to allow a later departure.

habits.boundary_condition: This is a soft preference: the evidence supports Delta as a favored option, not as the only acceptable airline or an always-first choice over every other preferred carrier.
habits.condition: When choosing among flight carriers and Delta is available while also satisfying the trip's schedule, route, price, and stop constraints.
habits.default_action: Search for or present Delta options as part of the preferred carrier set, and favor Delta when it is otherwise comparable to alternatives.
habits.exception_condition: Use another acceptable carrier when Delta is unavailable, materially worse, or does not meet the current trip constraints.
habits.name: Delta as a soft preferred carrier option
habits.preference_value: Delta is a preferred airline to include in the flight shortlist, but not an exclusive carrier requirement.
habits.scope_condition: Commercial flights originating from or returning to her Atlanta home base when multiple carriers satisfy the trip constraints.

habits.boundary_condition: Applies only to seat location. If seat selection is unavailable at booking or is deferred until check-in, note that limitation and try to secure a window seat at the earliest available time.
habits.condition: When booking or selecting seats for flights where a seat location preference can be applied.
habits.default_action: Prefer or request a window seat by default.
habits.exception_condition: Use a different seat only if the user specifies another seat preference, needs a different seating arrangement, or no acceptable window seat is available.
habits.name: prefers_window_seat_on_flights
habits.preference_value: window seat
habits.scope_condition: Seat selection for her recurring solo work flights and occasional personal flights when seat choice is available.

habits.boundary_condition: Apply this per room and do not infer it from the number of travelers or requested rooms.
habits.condition: When selecting a shared hotel room without an explicit request for separate beds.
habits.default_action: Prefer a room with a queen-size bed; a king-size bed may be accepted when offered as a larger alternative.
habits.exception_condition: Honor explicit twin-bed, separate-bed, or other room-specific sleeping arrangements instead.
habits.name: queen_bed_for_shared_hotel_room
habits.preference_value: Prefer a queen-size bed for a shared hotel room when no separate-bed arrangement is requested.
habits.scope_condition: Personal trips where Avery and her wife book one shared hotel room and have not requested separate beds.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat walking distance as the reusable threshold; use a stricter walk-time limit only when the current request explicitly supplies one
habits.condition: When searching for a hotel in a coastal or beach-oriented area
habits.default_action: Prioritize properties on the beach or close enough to walk while also filtering to the trip's stated budget
habits.exception_condition: Do not apply this preference to non-coastal trips or when the current trip names a different location priority
habits.name: Prefer beach-proximate hotels
habits.preference_value: A hotel on or near the beach, ideally within walking distance
habits.scope_condition: The couple's recurring beach-oriented vacation when comparing hotels within the stated trip budget.

habits.boundary_condition: Use a 3.5 minimum when the search is explicitly budget-focused. Apply either threshold only to the rating metric under discussion, and do not conflate hotel class, Google ratings, and customer-review ratings.
habits.condition: When a hotel search calls for a well-rated property and frames the stay as nice, upscale, resort-style, or explicitly budget-focused.
habits.default_action: Filter or prioritize options meeting a 4.0 minimum for nice, upscale, or resort-style searches, and identify the rating source when known.
habits.exception_condition: Follow any newly stated threshold or metric. If no suitable option meets the applicable floor while satisfying more important trip constraints, ask before relaxing it.
habits.name: contextual_hotel_rating_floor
habits.preference_value: Prefer hotels rated at least 4.0 when seeking a nice, upscale, or resort-style stay; for explicitly budget-focused searches, prefer at least 3.5.
habits.scope_condition: Annual coastal leisure searches framed as a nice, upscale, or resort-style stay, and any explicitly budget-focused variant of that search.

longitudinal_plan.travel_tempo: Roughly one work trip per month, with occasional clusters around exhibition openings, several personal visits, and one longer coastal vacation each year.
longitudinal_plan.typical_episode_shape: Most episodes span two to four sessions: establish fixed dates and commitments, compare flights, refine the return leg or seat, and then select lodging. Coastal planning episodes run longer, often five to seven sessions, because destinations, beach access, ratings, and room options are revisited before booking; some later sessions cover changes, verification, or cancellation decisions.

persona.household: Lives with her wife; they share hotel rooms on several family visits and take one coastal vacation most years.
persona.name: Avery Thompson
persona.planning_behavior: She starts with installation dates, museum access hours, or family commitments, then narrows flights by routing and timing before considering carrier and seat details. She chooses practical work lodging quickly, but compares coastal hotels more deliberately for walkability, ratings, and room configuration.
persona.travel_pattern: Avery travels about monthly to oversee exhibition installations, courier handoffs, and lender walkthroughs in major U.S. cities. These trips usually last two to four nights and involve fixed museum access windows, so she values simple flight itineraries and a useful final day. Personal travel includes visits to relatives and a carefully planned annual beach trip with her wife, where hotel location and quality receive more attention than they do on work stays.

travel_contexts.description: Recurring two- to four-night domestic trips tied to fixed installation, courier, or lender schedules.
Family visits and city breaks with her wife, usually in one shared hotel room.
A longer beach-oriented trip planned well ahead, with greater attention to hotel setting and quality.
